canonical_levels.CONFIRMED: Targeted static body or exact read-only layout/body query with corroborating structure, xref, or second static source; still not runtime truth.
canonical_levels.INFERRED: Bounded semantic interpretation from static names, layouts, call shape, or cross-artifact agreement; undocumented behavior remains open.
canonical_levels.OBSERVED_CURRENT: Direct current OpenSpore source, test, fixture, or clean-room projection; establishes current behavior only.
canonical_levels.SUPPORTED: Direct structure, interface surface, committed dossier, or multi-source static agreement supports a bounded claim without runtime confirmation.
canonical_levels.UNKNOWN: The available evidence is absent, contradictory, or insufficient for the bounded claim.
canonical_levels.VERIFIED: Direct current implementation, committed test, frozen export, pinned read-only query, or deterministic artifact comparison for the stated bounded claim; not automatically original runtime truth.

precedence: Pinned binary, export, SDK, and read-only query identity for bounded static facts
Committed source, tests, and fixtures for current OpenSpore behavior
Committed research and dossiers for cross-track synthesis
Derived knowledge-graph projections and triage for topology and prioritization
Unresolved or contradicted claims remain explicitly qualified
evidence_policy.runtime_rule: No original-process gameplay, editor, save, or load trace is available in the input set. No SDK name, static decompilation, structure layout, or current OpenSpore behavior is promoted to original runtime truth.
evidence_policy.sdk_rule: SDK names, sizes, offsets, enums, vtables, and method surfaces are static evidence; they do not independently prove undocumented behavior, exact function identity, or runtime ownership.
evidence_policy.decompilation_rule: Static decompilation is used only for bounded mechanics and provenance. No decompiled code is copied or reproduced.
evidence_policy.deduplication_rule: Repeated claims are merged only when the bounded statement and layer are the same; conflicting representations remain in contradictions rather than being silently chosen.
evidence_policy.array_order: All arrays use stable ID, path, package, or rank order; set-like string arrays are lexicographically sorted.
evidence_policy.key_order: Top-level keys follow the required schema order; nested objects use the stable field order shown in this ledger.

normalized_findings.statement: The committed evidence set contains no positive original-process runtime trace for Cell, editor, Empire, Space, or save/load behavior; undocumented original behavior remains static projection only.

The current OpenSpore resource seam verifies DBPF v3 record identity and extent to raw or QFS-decompressed bytes with exact type/group/instance lookup in one borrowed package; it is not original multi-package manager behavior.

The original resource subsystem exposes database, factory, type mapping, cache, reload, notification, and stream surfaces, but database priority, asynchronous completion, cache lifetime, and original load order are not reconstructed.

DBPF conceptual/current row identity is type/group/instance, while the pinned ResourceKey memory layout is instanceID/typeID/groupID; conversions must be explicit and positional serialization is unsafe.

The recovered Cell content family consists of direct fixed or count-driven records with explicit TypeIDs, byte spans, preserved pointer-shaped serialization slots, and validated or soft references; these are content schemas rather than generic save envelopes.

cCellGlobalsResource, direct Cell content records, cCellGame live pools, and cCellSerializableData are separate layers; a live serializable candidate does not prove content persistence or cross-stage handoff.

cCellDataReference_ is a static/runtime lazy reference cache keyed by instance ID and serializer, with a resource pointer and use counter; ownership fields are not proven file fields and its resource-manager selection contract remains bounded.
CellWorld and CellPopulate carry scale, population, count, size, z, and reference data but no recovered per-entity x/y field; original coordinate generation and actor materialization remain unknown.

Static Cell evidence supports a 4096-entry cCellObjectData pool, foreground/background query state, model/resource identity, GFX association, health, and mode lifecycle boundaries; exact runtime order and ownership correlation are not observed.

OpenSpore's Cell path is a clean-room bounded projection: typed content decoders, selected CellGame state, local deterministic CellSim behavior, world tokens, and a host renderer exist, but the original active-update orchestrator, exact GFX ownership, and end-to-end equivalence do not.

GMDL support is strongest for a current version-8 renderable prefix; version-9 framing is documented or oracle-described but unsupported by current C++, and the real cell-family trailer is accepted as opaque or best-effort rather than byte-exactly reconstructed.

RW4 support is a validated container directory: magic, manifest, type table, section-info rows, bounds, and BaseResource offset adjustment; section payload schemas, material, compiled-state, animation, skeleton, skin, and pixel execution remain unresolved.

Texture and material metadata is separated from gameplay predicates: Cell query geometry uses position and size, health UI uses live GFX and health, and effectMap is a gameplay-to-presentation bridge; no direct texture-to-team, selection, visibility, or collision path is established.

The 0x0F43029A world-object record is a distinct model-group or part-definition record with versions 9 and 10, extracted names and vector-like values, and complete current byte accounting; exact c-entry grammar, model ownership, and placement semantics are unresolved.

No literal original EditorData type or wire format was recovered; static evidence supports a composite model separating authored creature/resource/part data from transient cEditor, pose, UI, history, animation-world, and derived-skin state.

Persistence is layered: PropertyList and ClassSerializer expose typed property/object serialization surfaces, cCellSerializableData is a runtime persistence candidate, cGamePersistenceManager is a named service with LoadGame, and DBPF is a content-record container; exact PROP/SPO framing, ordering, migration, and survival are unknown.

major_relationships.statement: A DBPF row is selected by type/group/instance and yields bounded payload bytes; QFS is current verified extraction behavior, while original package precedence and write integration are separate.
A serializer-associated instance reference lazily resolves resource bytes, which are then interpreted by a TypeID-specific Cell schema; ownership linkage is not the content wire schema.

observations.claim: DBPF/current lookup is type, group, instance; SDK ResourceKey memory is instanceID, typeID, groupID.
Some persistence wording uses a different declaration order.

contradictions.adjudication: Use T:G:I for the DBPF conceptual row and current provider contract, and instance/type/group for the pinned 12-byte ResourceKey memory layout. Add explicit conversion; never infer wire order from one representation.

observations.claim: SDK describes a 20-byte Property with a value union and later flags/type offsets.
Imported Ghidra Property is 4 bytes with flags/type.

contradictions.adjudication: Neither layout is promoted to authoritative runtime or wire representation. Preserve both source-specific claims until allocation-size, constructor, getter, and typed value evidence resolves them.

observations.claim: Historical wording associated Cell records with a name/ID envelope.
Direct globals and other TypeID-specific Cell records are fixed/count-driven.

contradictions.adjudication: Reject the historical envelope claim for recovered direct Cell records. Retain CellSerializer as metadata/lazy-reference architecture for unresolved families; do not invent a generic wire envelope for direct schemas.

observations.claim: SDK/layout wording describes strength, variance, and period as int-like.
Direct Cell bytes and current decoder establish float32.

contradictions.adjudication: Use float32 for the bounded file decoder and preserve the SDK declaration mismatch as unresolved typing drift. Do not generalize it to all original consumers.

observations.claim: SDK labels are often wrappers, interior offsets, or containing bodies.
Current Ghidra boundaries disagree with several lifecycle and serializer anchors.

contradictions.adjudication: Retain SDK address/name pairs as SDK anchors. Attach behavior only to exact current entries or explicitly labeled mechanics-only regions; do not collapse anchors and entries.

observations.claim: Historical wording identifies 0x00E4CE20 as the globals accessor or loader.
Later read-only evidence describes 0x00E4CE20 as teardown/cache invalidation and 0x00E4CE40 as the typed accessor.

contradictions.adjudication: Do not implement 0x00E4CE20 as a getter. Preserve its later bounded teardown behavior, use 0x00E4CE40 for the typed accessor, and retain historical wording as provenance.

observations.claim: Some documentation/header wording implies strict full-record accounting.
Current C++ and tests treat trailer reads as best-effort and accept opaque remaining bytes.

contradictions.adjudication: Use the current implementation: strict version/geometry/material prefix and best-effort trailer. Treat older strict wording as stale for current C++; do not claim complete animation or trailer reconstruction.

observations.claim: Python oracle/documentation describes a version-9 variation.
Current C++ accepts only version 8.

contradictions.adjudication: Record v9 as documented/oracle evidence and unsupported current C++ behavior. Do not describe the current parser as v9-capable.

observations.claim: Header prose can suggest complete known-type validation.
Current implementation accepts unknown type codes informationally.

contradictions.adjudication: Use the implementation: RW4 complete() validates structure and bounds, not every type code. Unknown codes are current behavior, not successful semantic decode.

observations.claim: The record extracts part names and vectors and has no current runtime consumer.
Historical notes suggested Cell-soup placement, but recovered marker and scene evidence do not establish it.

contradictions.adjudication: Use model-group/part-definition classification. Reject the claim that this record is itself Cell scene placement; retain exact body grammar and loader ownership as unknown.

contradictions.topic: Cell pool liveness, query storage, and current entities

observations.claim: Original cCellObjectData is a runtime field shape while current CellPool and CellSim are bounded projections.
Current CellGame and CellSim are parallel representations and are not integrated in the frame loop.

contradictions.adjudication: Keep pool allocation, mIsIdle, fixture alive, current Entity.alive, original query links, and current vector/LIFO behavior separate. Do not claim byte or semantic identity.

observations.claim: Current effect and presentation seams exist as bounded host projections.
Semantic verification records that CellAnim/effect helpers are not an integrated original pose/effect pipeline.

contradictions.adjudication: Keep current GFX preload, host draw, and helper tests as partial current behavior. Do not promote them to original animation, pose, skeleton, effect, or pixel equivalence.

observations.claim: Current-only labels include CellImages at 0x40616201 and PaletteModels at 0x406B6200.
Tests describe 0x40616201 as a cell-model LOD group and SDK mapping places Palettes at 0x406B6A00.

contradictions.adjudication: Quarantine current-only conflicting labels. Retain exact SDK group identities and raw numeric IDs when semantics are not independently established.

observations.claim: SDK/export names cCreatureGameData+0x08 as an integer-like flap field.
Static writes to the corresponding global use float-sized operations.

contradictions.adjudication: Retain the SDK field label as an export claim, mark runtime type and semantic identity unresolved, and do not use it as a current or original serialization field.

contradictions.topic: Missing SaveGame symbol versus save capability

observations.claim: Read-only searches did not find a named SaveGame, Profile, or Slot entry.
Persistence manager, PropertyList, ClassSerializer, saved header, and serializable interfaces establish a save/load architecture.

contradictions.adjudication: Do not infer that saving is absent. Treat named writer/profile/slot functions as unresolved and retain the architecture as static evidence only.

observations.claim: SDK, xref, and decompilation surfaces support inferred lifecycle descriptions despite no transition trace.
Runtime ordering is explicitly unknown and static projections are retained.

contradictions.adjudication: Promote bounded static layouts, direct current behavior, and explicit negative evidence only within their stated layer. Keep undocumented runtime ordering, selection, placement, event, and save behavior UNKNOWN or INFERRED.

proven_or_refuted_assumptions.assumption: Recovered direct Cell records use a CellSerializer name/ID envelope.
proven_or_refuted_assumptions.rationale: Direct fixed/count-driven TypeID-specific layouts support content bytes without that envelope; generic CellSerializer framing remains unknown for other families.

proven_or_refuted_assumptions.assumption: DBPF identity can be serialized as an unlabelled positional triple without conversion.
proven_or_refuted_assumptions.rationale: The current DBPF row order and ResourceKey memory order differ; explicit named conversion is required.

proven_or_refuted_assumptions.assumption: OpenSpore IResourceProvider is equivalent to original cResourceManager orchestration.
proven_or_refuted_assumptions.rationale: The provider is a narrow one-package or memory byte seam; database registration, priority, factories, cache, reload, notifications, and property orchestration are outside it.

proven_or_refuted_assumptions.assumption: Synthetic fixtures and generated manifests are original-game or save/load oracles.
proven_or_refuted_assumptions.rationale: The artifacts explicitly classify fixtures as current OpenSpore regression or synthetic format evidence only.

proven_or_refuted_assumptions.assumption: The current GMDL parser completely reconstructs all original GMDL versions, trailers, and animation data.
proven_or_refuted_assumptions.rationale: Current C++ accepts v8 only, retains a strict renderable prefix, and treats the real-family trailer as opaque or best-effort.

proven_or_refuted_assumptions.assumption: The current RW4 structural reader decodes section payloads and material or animation semantics.
proven_or_refuted_assumptions.rationale: The current reader exposes a validated section directory and adjusted BaseResource address but leaves payloads opaque.

proven_or_refuted_assumptions.assumption: 0x0F43029A is a verified per-entity Cell scene-placement record.
proven_or_refuted_assumptions.rationale: Resolved research classifies it as model-group/part-definition data; exact loader ownership remains unknown, so a different future linkage is not ruled out.

proven_or_refuted_assumptions.assumption: Texture or material identity is proven to encode team, selection, visibility, collision, or faction state.
proven_or_refuted_assumptions.rationale: Available evidence separates query geometry, health UI, effects, and empire identity color; no direct texture-to-predicate path is established.

proven_or_refuted_assumptions.assumption: Current growMeter is the original evolution-points, unlocked-parts, or saved progression field.
proven_or_refuted_assumptions.rationale: The current growMeter is a local deterministic Cell contract counter; original progression is split across cCreatureGameData and cCellSerializableData fields.

proven_or_refuted_assumptions.assumption: cCellGlobalsResource and cCellSerializableData are the same record or save object.
proven_or_refuted_assumptions.rationale: Globals is a direct 276-byte content and tuning record; cCellSerializableData is a separate 236-byte runtime progression and state candidate held by cCellGame.

proven_or_refuted_assumptions.assumption: The absence of a named SaveGame, Profile, or Slot function proves that saving does not exist.
proven_or_refuted_assumptions.rationale: Persistence architecture, vtables, property codecs, saved headers, and serializer surfaces remain; unnamed or virtual paths may exist.

proven_or_refuted_assumptions.assumption: SDK names and static decompilation alone prove exact runtime behavior.
proven_or_refuted_assumptions.rationale: The evidence policy and source tracks explicitly bound SDK names, anchors, layouts, and static bodies; runtime claims require independent behavioral evidence.

provenance.read_scope: All 14 JSON artifacts in knowledgegraph/research/data-model/ were read in full; no additional research was needed beyond their directly cited provenance and bounded source references.
method: Read the 14 input JSON artifacts as the authoritative reconciliation set.
Normalize repeated claims into stable findings without promoting static SDK, Ghidra, decompilation, or current source evidence to original runtime truth.
Record cross-track conflicts explicitly and choose only representation-safe or current-source adjudications.
Preserve source artifact paths and anchor references for every finding, relationship, centrality item, contradiction, assumption, and gap.
Sort arrays by stable IDs, package IDs, paths, or rank and use fixed nested field order.
constraints: No SPORE files were inspected or modified.
No source, Ghidra program, historical triage, or input artifact was modified.
No proprietary asset, binary, SDK source, or decompiled code was copied.
Runtime claims are limited to the committed evidence set and remain unverified where no positive original trace exists.
